overview: Iron Mountain is a global REIT that stores, protects, and manages physical records and digital/physical IT assets for enterprise and government customers, operating roughly 1,400+ facilities across ~60 countries. Its legacy Global RIM (Records and Information Management) business — physical document storage, secure shredding, and data management — still generates the bulk of revenue and cash flow, while a fast-growing Global Data Center segment plus newer Asset Lifecycle Management (ALM, including IT asset disposition) and Digital Solutions businesses are now the primary growth engines. The company elected REIT status in 2014 and pays a quarterly dividend funded from Adjusted Funds From Operations (AFFO).

business_model.summary: Highly recurring storage-rental revenue (records boxes billed per cubic foot/unit regardless of activity) plus service revenue (retrieval, destruction, digitization, ALM/IT-asset disposition, and data center colocation/wholesale leasing). Storage economics are the moat: once records are boxed and shelved, customers rarely retrieve or relocate them, so storage revenue is extremely sticky and high-margin, while data center and ALM are faster-growing but more capital- and competition-intensive.

revenue_streams.name: Global RIM - Services (retrieval, destruction, data management)

business_model.customer_type: B2B enterprise and government — large multinationals, healthcare, financial services, legal, life sciences, and hyperscale/enterprise data center tenants; long-dated (typically 15-20yr) records storage relationships and multi-year data center leases
business_model.geographic_mix: North America largest market by revenue, with substantial and growing international operations (Europe, Latin America, Asia-Pacific including India/Chennai, Western Europe/Amsterdam data center campuses)

competitive_position.market_position: Dominant global leader in physical records and information management (low-single-digit organic growth, highly fragmented but IRM is the largest player by scale and density of facilities); a smaller, rapidly scaling challenger in data centers (~4-5% share) against specialist giants Equinix and Digital Realty

moat_factors.description: Physical records, once boxed and shelved, are rarely moved; relocation cost and operational disruption of migrating millions of boxes/cubic feet deters customer churn, supporting >98% customer retention historically and durable pricing power on storage rental rates

moat_factors.factor: Scale and density of real estate network
moat_factors.description: ~1,400+ facilities across ~60 countries gives logistics, pricing, and service-breadth advantages smaller regional records competitors cannot match
Deep enterprise records relationships are being leveraged to sell ALM (IT asset disposition/data destruction), digital transformation (DXP/AI), and data center services to the same customer base

Growing rapidly (targeting ~1.4GW from ~500MW current operating base) but still a small share versus Equinix/Digital Realty, competing for power, land, and capital against better-capitalized specialists
Chain-of-custody, data destruction certification, and regulatory compliance (healthcare/financial records retention) create a trust-based barrier for new entrants in regulated verticals

weaknesses: Legacy records storage volumes are structurally declining in some mature markets as digitization reduces net physical box adds
Data center segment is capital-intensive and competing against far larger, better-capitalized pure-play data center REITs for power, land, and hyperscale tenants
High financial leverage (negative/near-zero shareholders' equity) limits balance-sheet flexibility relative to data center peers
ALM/IT asset disposition is a lower-margin, more commoditized, and more competitive business than storage

growth_drivers: Data center capacity expansion: targeting ~1.4GW of total capacity (nearly tripling the current operating base of ~500MW), with 325-400MW scheduled to energize over the next 18-24 months, driven by AI/hyperscale demand
Asset Lifecycle Management (ALM) scaling into a targeted multibillion-dollar business, up 63% in 2025 (40% organic) and guided to ~$850M in 2026
Digital Solutions and AI-enabled platform (Insight DXP, agentic AI document processing) growing recurring, higher-margin digital revenue, now >45% of total revenue
Pricing power in legacy storage rental business (consistent mid-single-digit annual price increases on a largely captive customer base)
Cross-selling data center, ALM, and digital services into the existing enterprise/government records customer base
International expansion of data centers (India/Chennai, Amsterdam campus expansion, Virginia/Richmond/Manassas capacity additions)

business.risk: Secular decline in physical records volumes
business.description: Enterprise digitization reduces net new box adds in some mature markets over the long term, though churn remains very low

Competing for power, land, and hyperscale tenants against far larger and better-capitalized specialists (Equinix, Digital Realty); execution risk on signing/energizing ~900MW+ of planned/under-construction capacity
No single customer risk disclosed as material, but large data center leases carry tenant concentration and renewal risk

financial.description: Stockholders' equity was negative (~-$1.39B as of Q3 2026, versus -$981M at FY2025 and -$503M at FY2024), with total debt of ~$18.0B; heavy reliance on continued debt/equity capital markets access to fund the data center buildout

2026 capex guided at ~$2.2B, overwhelmingly for growth (data centers); funding gap between AFFO/dividend payout and growth capex requires ongoing external capital raises, exposing the company to capital-markets and interest-rate conditions
A portion of debt (reported near ~20%+) is variable-rate; meaningful debt maturities in coming years require refinancing in prevailing rate environments
Meaningful international revenue (EUR, GBP, AUD, and other currencies) creates translation and transaction FX exposure

regulatory.description: Must continue to satisfy REIT distribution and asset/income tests; failure to do so (including due to debt covenant distribution limits) could jeopardize favorable tax treatment
Operates under data protection, chain-of-custody, and secure-destruction regulatory regimes across many jurisdictions; compliance failures carry reputational and liability risk
Local power-grid capacity constraints, permitting, and environmental/energy regulations can delay or increase the cost of planned data center capacity additions

macro.description: As a highly levered REIT reliant on debt-funded growth capex, rising rates increase financing costs and can compress the capex funding math and valuation multiple
Data center growth thesis depends on continued hyperscale/AI infrastructure demand; a slowdown in AI capex cycles could impair leasing velocity and returns on the capacity buildout
Faster-growing services businesses (ALM, digital transformation projects) are more discretionary/project-based than core storage and could soften in an economic downturn

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Legacy records/information management is a mature, low-single-digit-growth, high-cash-generation industry; data center/digital infrastructure is a high-growth segment benefiting from AI/hyperscale demand but facing power and land constraints industry-wide
macro_factors.cyclicality: Core records storage is highly non-cyclical/defensive (recurring, low-churn revenue); newer growth segments (data center leasing, ALM, digital projects) carry more cyclicality tied to enterprise IT spending and AI infrastructure investment cycles
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: High — heavily levered balance sheet with negative book equity and large ongoing debt-funded growth capex program; REIT valuation multiples are also sensitive to rate levels
key_input_costs: Real estate/land acquisition and construction costs

recent_developments.event: Record Q3 revenue of $1,990.6M (+13.5% YoY); net income $128.9M; Adjusted EBITDA $748.0M (37.6% margin); AFFO $458.4M ($1.53/share, up from $1.32/share in Q3 2025); data center/digital/ALM collectively grew >30% YoY

Raised full-year 2026 guidance: revenue to $7,950-8,020M (~16% growth), Adjusted EBITDA to $2,948-2,978M, AFFO to $1,780-1,800M, AFFO/share to $5.94-6.00 (~15% growth) - all raised from prior guidance set in August
Quarterly dividend raised 15% to $0.993/share, payable January 6, 2027
Leased 102MW of new data center capacity in the quarter, bringing year-to-date leasing to 137MW; continuing build-out toward a ~1.4GW total capacity target (from ~500MW currently operating)

Expanded planned data center capacity in Virginia by 350+MW via new Richmond/Manassas site acquisitions; topped out structural build of Chennai, India data center; announced Amsterdam campus expansion

ALM (Asset Lifecycle Management/IT asset disposition) revenue scaling rapidly - up 63% in 2025 (40% organic), guided to ~$850M in 2026, with management targeting a multibillion-dollar business over time
Launched/scaled Insight DXP, an AI-powered agentic document processing platform; digital recurring revenue now >45% of total company revenue; won large AI-driven digitization contracts
2026 capex guided at ~$2.2B, overwhelmingly directed to data center and growth-business capacity, funded via continued debt issuance alongside operating cash flow

Analyst price targets raised through the year (e.g., JPMorgan to $138 from $121 in May 2026; Wells Fargo to $135 in April 2026) on data center growth optimism, though stock saw volatility/pullbacks tied to capex funding and execution concerns

Raised from prior $1,760-1,780M range set in August 2026; ~16% YoY growth
Management guided to >25% growth in data center revenue for 2026
Follows 63% growth (40% organic) in 2025; management targets ALM becoming a multibillion-dollar business longer-term
Predominantly growth capex for data center capacity buildout
Implied by full-year guide; Q4 Adjusted EBITDA ~$780M, AFFO ~$473M, AFFO/share ~$1.57

guidance.management_commentary: CEO William Meaney described the business outlook as 'strong with a clear view for sustained long-term growth,' citing accelerating cross-sell momentum in ALM and Digital Solutions as a key driver of future growth alongside the data center buildout. Management reiterated the long-term target of growing data center capacity toward ~1.4GW (from the current ~500MW operating base), with 325-400MW scheduled to energize over the next 18-24 months.

bull_case: Core records storage business is a highly defensive, recurring-revenue cash cow with near-zero churn and consistent pricing power, funding the dividend and much of the growth capex
Data center segment is scaling rapidly (>25% revenue growth guided for 2026) with a large contracted/signed pipeline (137MW leased YTD 2026) riding the AI/hyperscale infrastructure demand wave

ALM and Digital Solutions are high-growth, higher-margin diversification plays (ALM +63% in 2025, guided to ~$850M in 2026; digital recurring revenue now >45% of total) reducing reliance on legacy storage
Management has consistently raised full-year AFFO and revenue guidance through 2026, and just raised the dividend 15%, signaling confidence in cash flow durability

Deep, long-tenured enterprise/government customer relationships provide a built-in cross-sell channel for newer growth businesses, lowering customer acquisition costs relative to pure-play data center REITs
bear_case: Negative/deeply negative shareholders' equity (~-$1.39B as of Q3 2026) and ~$18B of debt leave little balance-sheet cushion; the growth strategy depends on continuous access to debt and equity capital markets at favorable terms

Data center capex program (~$2.2B guided for 2026, growing) is being funded against a legacy business with only modest organic growth, raising execution and returns-on-capital risk if leasing pace or pricing disappoints

IRM is a sub-scale challenger in data centers against far larger, better-capitalized specialists (Equinix, Digital Realty) competing for the same power, land, and hyperscale tenants, with no guarantee of achieving target returns on the ~900MW+ of planned capacity
Rising or persistently elevated interest rates would increase financing costs on a highly levered balance sheet and could compress REIT valuation multiples broadly

Legacy records/storage volumes face long-term secular digitization headwinds, meaning an increasing share of consolidated growth must come from faster-growing but less-proven, more competitive segments (data center, ALM, digital)
